chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Ishkuri) he said: Al-Nakha'i narrated to me from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who is in the state of Ihram: if the sun strikes him and it is difficult for him and he becomes dizzy, so he seeks shelter from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He knows himself best; if he knows that the sun will not reach him (cause harm), let him seek shade from it.'

key_terms.أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ: He knows himself best (referring to personal assessment of harm)
key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who needs to seek shade from the sun due to heat or dizziness?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the principle of *al-‘ilaj bi-ma yudarru* (removing harm) for a pilgrim suffering from intense heat, ruling that seeking shade is permissible as long as it is done to alleviate genuine distress rather than to avoid the sun entirely. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing ritual purity with physical well-being, distinguishing between mere discomfort and actual harm that necessitates relief.
